Q: Is there any way to programatically tell if a Summary Task is collapsed? A:

There aren't any properties like that, perhaps because how the tasks are displayed is separate from the task object itself. Give this a try:

Function IsSummaryCollapsed(uid As Long) As Boolean

    Dim curTask As Long
    curTask = ActiveCell.Task.UniqueID
    
    Find "UniqueID", "equals", uid
    
    Dim ol As String
    ol = ActiveCell.Task.OutlineNumber
    
    SelectTaskField Row:=1, Column:="Name"
    
    IsSummaryCollapsed = Not (ActiveCell.Task.OutlineNumber Like ol & ".*")
    
    Find "UniqueID", "equals", curTask
    
End Function

Note: if the uid is for a non-summary task, it will return True.

Q: "All columns in a tibble must be vectors" when attempting to connect to Databricks via `sparklyr::spark_connect` A:

Seems like it was an issue of incompatibility between Spark 4.1 and pysparklyr. After I raised a github ticket, the devs applied a fix; installing the updated dev version made it possible to connect again.

Q: How to make a multiple-read/single-write lock from more basic synchronization primitives? A: 
Maybe you can add a time ordered Que Next Index ?
This way Read & Writes are Rotated.
- Excuse my mixing of Python and C++ 


class shared_mutex
    ...
    int  CurQueBotIdx = 0 , CurQueTopIdx = 0 

private  Myidx

def sem_lock() :
    ;

def sem_unlock() :
    global  CurQueTopIdx 
    CurQueBotIdx ++


def  RequestReadWrite() :
    global  MyIdx , CurQueTopIdx 
    MyIdx = CurQueTopIdx 
    CurQueTopIdx ++ 

def  AwaitSemReadWriteAvail() :
    global  MyIdx , CurQueBotIdx 
    while ( CurQueBotIdx != MyIdx ) : 
        sleep(0.001)  // 1 ms or 0.000001 = 1us or whatever 
    sem_lock()
   
def main() :
    
    while ( 1 ) :

        ## do other work  

        ## need R/W Semaphore : 
        RequestReadWrite()
        AwaitSemReadWriteAvail()

        ## do Read / Write semaphore job 

        sem_unlock()

        sleep(0.001)  // 1 ms or 0.000001 = 1us or whatever

Q: Ellipsis text-overflow not working / broken A:

Multiline text with auto-wrapping, being prerequisite for ellipsis, as well as basically all white-space and even overflow CSS properties of text nodes are all newcomers to SVG coming along with the "new" SVG2, if we can use that word for a spec that originates from 2012.

As of 2026, there is (still) little to no progress in SVG2 adoption among major browsers in this particular area (*).

Even humbly looking white-space alone has diverging outcomes between browsers as of now:

<svg style="background: mark">
  <text y="20" style="white-space: pre-line">
   Foo
   Bar
Baz
  </text>
</svg>

This will show you three lines in Firefox, but single line in Chrome.

As C3roe mentioned, the specification pages are "faking" the illustrations of the code snippets outcomes, for a pretty clear reason: simply to deliver the intended outcome to readers that are using browsers with currently supported subset of SVG. Using the "baseline" SVG seems like pragmatic choice, considering that the only alternative could be embedding raster pictures. It might seem misleading, but really makes sense: they do not document the present they try to describe the future.

(*) See https://wpt.fyi/results/svg/text/reftests It might be a bit better among SVG authoring software, for example Inkscape can at least auto-wrap text during authoring, but outputs positioned tspans in the resulting document, probably for pragmatic compatibility reasons.
